rationale: The adverse-phase receipt answered the last open question and answered it negatively, with witnesses rather than an absence of evidence: the comparison that predicted an overlap in the uniform case came back violated with all twenty adverse trials as valid witnesses, and the same twenty trials show that the isolated voter never reached a higher term at all - it stayed a Candidate at the leader's own term, which is pre-vote holding an isolated node at its term because it cannot assemble a majority to pre-vote for it. That both confirms the separation recorded earlier for uniform settings and explains the path by which the mixed-timer configuration escapes it, so this submission records the interpretation, promotes the mechanism as knowledge with the receipt as its evidence, and marks the question answered.

knowledge.statement: Two gates keep an isolated voter from displacing a leader whose lease is still running when every node shares its timer settings. A node that knows a leader refuses a vote request from any other candidate before it compares terms, so a candidate cannot collect the vote of a peer that still has the leader in view; and with pre-vote enabled the candidate does not raise its term at all while it cannot assemble a majority, because runCandidate's pre-vote phase keeps the node at its current term and only elects for real after the pre-vote is won. Both gates are released by the same event - a peer losing the leader from view when its own heartbeat timer expires - and that timer is reset by the same leader whose lease is expiring, so with shared settings the lease expires no later than the earliest moment at which a vote could be granted.
knowledge.conditions: Pre-vote enabled (the captured default), sending nodes sharing their timer settings, the candidate isolated from the leader and from a majority of voters, and ValidateConfig's per-node relation LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout holding on every node.

interpretations.rationale: Retained execution (check 666b1f50481d4784a6fe2bac4fe4131e, exit 0, tests_passed, 72 parsed events, 0 parse errors; twenty-two hand-built four-node clusters with identical settings, one per trial). Comparison 0, which predicted that a voter already campaigning before the isolation would overlap the cut-off leader's confirmation with its election, came back violated and comparison_complete, with all twenty adverse trials as valid witnesses: none of them produced a confirmation after a competing leader existed, and none of them produced a competing leader during the confirmation window at all. Comparison 1 held for the two plain controls, which also saw no competing leader. The same twenty trials explain why, and the explanation is more precise than the source reading I recorded earlier: preexisting_candidate is false in every adverse trial, and the isolated voter's final state is Candidate at the leader's own term (2 or 3 against a leader at the same term) rather than at a higher one. That is pre-vote: runCandidate's pre-vote phase leaves the node at its current term and only starts a real election after the pre-vote is won, so a node that cannot reach a majority never raises its term, let alone wins; and when a peer does become willing to pre-vote, that willingness comes from losing the leader from view, which cannot happen before its own heartbeat timer expires. With shared settings that timer is at least as long as the leader's lease, so the leader stops confirming before any vote could be counted, which is exactly what the confirmations show: eighteen to twenty-one per trial, the last at 47-58ms, in every case with no competing leader to follow them. The suspicion this question was opened to test is therefore refuted for the uniform configuration, and the mixed-timer finding keeps its scope: an inequality between a voter's election timeout and the leader's lease is what lets a node get ahead of the lease, and no amount of adverse history inside a uniformly configured cluster reproduces it.
counterevidence: The test was constructed by isolating one voter rather than by catching a cluster in which a real campaign was already under way, and pre-vote prevented the higher-term candidacy from forming at all, so the run cannot separate the two gates' contributions: it confirms the separation but attributes it to the combination rather than to either gate alone.

Pre-vote is what the captured default enables; a cluster running with PreVoteDisabled would let an isolated voter raise its term, and this run did not measure that configuration, though the known-leader gate would still apply to its vote requests.
The confirmation counts here (eighteen to twenty-one per trial, ending at 47-58ms) are the uniform case's lease window, not evidence about behaviour after the lease expires.
As in every run of this family, no application read is served, so what is measured is the coexistence of a confirmation with a competing leader rather than a delivered value.
limitations: One cluster shape (three voters plus one nonvoter, quorum two) with identical settings at 50ms, in one process with in-memory transports.
The adverse history reaches only as far as isolating one voter for up to three seconds; longer or multi-voter histories were not tried.
The negative result is about this snapshot's defaults (pre-vote enabled) and would need a repeat with pre-vote disabled to make any claim about implementations that turn it off.
